title: The code that runs, power-on to /sbin/init

steps.title: Open these files to follow the boot
steps.body: Four blocks, in boot order. Every path was checked against the pinned trees, and every row says in one line what the file does.

steps.title: The ROM has no source here
steps.body: It is mask ROM inside the chip, described in chapter 6 of the Zynq-7000 technical reference manual (UG585). The rest of this map starts where its output begins: a file in on-chip RAM.

steps.title: The SPL starts in board_init_f()
steps.body: `board_init_f()` calls `ps7_init()` before anything else; `spl_boot_device()` reads the SLCR boot-mode register and answers `BOOT_DEVICE_MMC1` for the SD card.

steps.title: How our ps7 file gets compiled in
steps.body: When `CONFIG_XILINX_PS_INIT_FILE` is set the Makefile compiles that file as `ps_init_gpl.o` into the SPL. Without the option it looks for `board/xilinx/zynq/<device-tree-name>/ps7_init_gpl.c`, which is how the boards in the U-Boot tree do it.

steps.title: Where BOOT.BIN is made
steps.body: `Makefile.xpl` runs `mkimage -T zynqimage` on the SPL binary; `zynqimage.c` writes the header the ROM reads. Read the comment at the top of that file for the layout.

steps.title: U-Boot proper learns where it booted from
steps.body: `board_late_init()` puts `mmc0` first in `boot_targets` when the boot-mode pins say SD, and `env_get_location()` puts the saved environment in a FAT file `uboot.env` on the same card.

steps.title: The distro boot script lives here
steps.body: `scan_dev_for_boot_part`, the `boot_prefixes` (`/` and `/boot/`) and `scan_dev_for_extlinux` are macros in this header; together they are why a plain `extlinux.conf` is enough.

steps.title: The last U-Boot line
steps.body: `do_bootz()` passes the address of the device tree in register r2 and jumps to the zImage: the 32-bit ARM boot protocol.

steps.title: Linux describes the SoC in a shared file
steps.body: Our board file includes it; it declares both Cortex-A9 cores, the clock controller, `uart0`, `sdhci0`, `gem0` and the `devcfg` FPGA manager. The board file switches on what the board uses and adds the board-specific wiring.

steps.title: The FPGA manager is built as a module
steps.body: It would load a PL bitstream; nothing calls it in this build, but it is the file to read before chapter 13.
